description: Capability for the main window. The six folder-sync permissions (M71, decision D37) are the ONLY filesystem grant this application has: they allow reading, writing, listing and deleting `.elrsp` profile files inside the ONE directory the user picks in the native folder dialog, and nothing else. The directory itself is granted at runtime by `folder-sync:allow-grant`, which canonicalises the picked path and REPLACES any previous grant; every other folder-sync command resolves a bare file name inside that single root and refuses separators, `..`, drive prefixes, absolute paths, reserved device names, symlinks and non-`.elrsp` names (see `folder_sync::resolve_in_root` in src/commands/config.rs). `tauri-plugin-fs` is deliberately not registered as a plugin, so no other filesystem reach exists in the ACL. The one write that happens outside it is `save_export_file` (v3.0.3, `commands/export.rs`), and it is built so there is nothing to grant: it opens the native save dialog ITSELF and writes only the path the user picked inside that same call, so the webview never names a destination — the alternative shape (`dialog.save()` in JS, then a Rust `write(path, contents)`) would have handed the frontend an arbitrary-path write that no ACL entry describes, since app-level commands are not ACL-gated at all. The three notification permissions (v3.0.3) follow the same named-not-default rule: `notification:default` would additionally grant thirteen scheduling, channel, listener and pending/active-query commands, NONE of which this app uses and none of which even exist on desktop — the plugin's `invoke_handler` registers exactly `notify`, `request_permission` and `is_permission_granted`, so the three named permissions below are the complete reach the live-alert feature needs.
